title: Weekly Update on Concerts and Testing
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
A Message From Dr. Cannon
Happy Friday!Our third graders had their concert on Wednesday evening and 4th graders attended Ag Day at the high school today to learn more about the agriculture program.3rd-5th grade students continue to work hard on their Ohio State Tests. Next week will be the last week of this state testing. 3rd and 4th graders will take their math test and 5th graders will take their science test. Kindergarten through third grades will take their spring MAP tests in the next few weeks as well.Have a great weekend!Sincerely,Dr. Kirsten Cannon, Principal

title: Lions Club Spring Eyeglass Collection Drive
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Lions Club Spring Eyeglass Collection
The Oxford Lions Club Sight Saving Committee is collecting used eyeglasses, sunglasses as well as cases! These glasses and cases are donated all over the world to children who are in need. The lenses and frames from the donated glasses are modified to meet individual children's eye needs. Every year, Oxford Lions Club collects and sends 900-plus pairs of glasses to children in need!Please send any glasses donations to Betsy Beaton (Marshall Elementary School) or Shaunna Tafelski (Board Office) by mid-May We are happy to swing by and pick up glasses donations or they can be dropped off at Marshall or the Board Office. Thank you for supporting the Oxford Lions Club! Thanks!

summary: The **Oxford Lions Club** is collecting used eyeglasses, sunglasses, and cases to donate to children in need worldwide. The club modifies donated lenses and frames to meet individual children's eye needs and sends **900+ pairs annually**. **Donations are due by mid-May** and can be sent to Betsy Beaton at Marshall Elementary School or Shaunna Tafelski at the Board Office, with pickup available upon request.

title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary: The school nurse provides a flowchart to help distinguish between allergy symptoms and cold symptoms. **Key differences**: Allergies typically involve clear mucus, seasonal occurrence, itchiness, and symptoms that last for extended periods. Colds usually present with green or yellow mucus, fever, body discomfort, and symptoms that come on quickly and taper off fairly rapidly. **Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

title: Allergies or Cold Decision Guide
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary: The school nurse provides a visual flowchart to help determine whether symptoms indicate allergies or a cold. Key differences: **allergies** typically cause itchy eyes/nose/throat, clear mucus, and symptoms that occur seasonally or persist for extended periods; **colds** typically cause green/yellow mucus, body discomfort, fever, and symptoms that come on fast and taper off quickly. **Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.
